_comment: How a word of a text in Egyptian Arabic is turned into something a dictionary can be asked about: the Egyptian dictionary first, the standard one after it, with these rules and then lib/lang/ar.lookup.json's (lib/lookup.py rules(): a variety's rules come first). The words Egyptian has and standard Arabic has not (دلوقتي, إزاي, عايز) are pages of the Egyptian dictionary and need no rule; these are the ones written onto a word standard Arabic also has: the present's b- (بيكتب, بتقول, بكتب), the future's ha- (هنروح, هيكتب), the negation's ma-...-š (ماكتبش, مابيكتبش), the pronoun written onto the verb with -l- (قولّي, كتبتلوش) and the hamza a text writes as a plain letter (تاكل, تقرا). Measured on TODOs/arabic-dialects/ar-egy.txt.

_article: THE ARTICLE IS TAKEN OFF HERE and not in ar.lookup.json: Wiktionary's standard Arabic files a word with its article among its forms, and its dialect dictionaries do not (الولاد, الدراري, للدار found nothing). A verb's prefix leaves three letters at least (`min_stem_length`): حالك is not the future's ح + الك.
